text:
sam: Heads-up — publish pipeline just failed for the py/ts SDKs during today's change window. Looks like npm returned a 403 for @redwood/sdk-ts and PyPI wheels failed checksum verification. deploy-bot already flagged the job.

deploy-bot: publish-job #1753: FAILED — npm: 403 Forbidden (publish), pypi: checksum mismatch on wheel. Artifacts archived to gs://ci-artifacts/sdk/1753/. Rollback actions blocked pending manual coord.

maya: On it. Is this within the 22:00-02:00 change window? Any live customers affected yet?

sam: Yes change window is active. Notified Customer Success to watch for SDK install errors but no major customer reports so far. Pasted the two snippets below.

sam: ```
npm ERR! code E403
npm ERR! 403 Forbidden - PUT https://registry.npmjs.org/@redwood%2Fsdk-ts - You do not have permission to publish

ERROR: Hash mismatch for redwood_sdk-1.4.3-py3-none-any.whl
Expected: sha256:abcdef...
Got: sha256:123456...
```

jon: 403 usually means token scope or rotation. Did CI use ephemeral tokens that might have rotated during the run? If token is bad we can't republish the same version on npm. For npm we can "promote" the previous release by moving the dist-tag. For PyPI, if wheel checksum is wrong we can rebuild and upload a hotfix patch (e.g., 1.4.4) and mark 1.4.3 as bad in release notes.

liz: We still have the previous artifacts in GCS (gs://ci-artifacts/sdk/1.4.2/). I can re-promote the npm package by setting the dist-tag to 1.4.2 if ops agrees. That avoids rollback of K8s or runtime work.

maya: Proposal: immediate mitigation steps —
1) npm: set dist-tag `latest` back to 1.4.2 so `npm install @redwood/sdk-ts` resolves to the safe version. Command: `npm dist-tag add @redwood/sdk-ts@1.4.2 latest`
2) PyPI: attempt rebuild of wheel with strict env and checksum verification; if rebuild works, publish as 1.4.4-hotfix and note in release notes that 1.4.3 is faulty.
3) Update release notes and send customer notification via #customer-success.
4) Hold other publishes in the change window until canary passes.

sam: I like that. Who takes npm dist-tag and who takes PyPI rebuild? Also please include a short blurb in release notes: "Do not use 1.4.3" and link to the issue.

maya: I can do the npm dist-tag roll back now. Will run dist-tag command and confirm.

jon: I'll rebuild the wheel locally in the clean CI image, verify sha256 locally, then upload with `twine upload dist/*` if verified. I will also push rebuilt artifacts to GCS for audit. If twine upload fails because PyPI rejects same version, I'll bump to 1.4.4-hotfix.

liz: I'll open a tiny PR to the docs to pin the yarn/npm install snippet to 1.4.2 and add a warning banner on the SDK page. Also will add an entry to the release notes draft: "DO NOT USE 1.4.3 — replaced by 1.4.2 (npm) / 1.4.4-hotfix (PyPI pending)".

deploy-bot: dist-tag change requested by @maya: enqueue job #1754 to run `npm dist-tag add @redwood/sdk-ts@1.4.2 latest`. ETA ~3m.

release-engineer: Good call to gate publishes. I'll lock the publish queue for the remainder of the change window (22:00-02:00 UTC) until canary verification completes. If canary fails we escalate to outage warroom.

maya: dist-tag command executed. `npm dist-tag add @redwood/sdk-ts@1.4.2 latest` -> success. Confirmed `npm dist-tag ls @redwood/sdk-ts` shows latest -> 1.4.2. Notified registry admin to check token rotation logs. :thumbsup:

sam: Awesome. jon, any ETA on the PyPI rebuild?

jon: Building now in the CI clean image. If checksum verification passes I'll upload in ~18m. If not, I'll cut 1.4.4-hotfix and upload, then update release notes. I'll post back with the artifact link.

liz: PR opened: docs update + release notes draft. Link: https://github.com/redwood/sdks/pull/782 (will mark as urgent).

sam: Notify sales & support once docs PR merged and dist-tag rollback confirmed. Also schedule a post-mortem tomorrow to capture root cause (token rotation vs CI signing issue).

deploy-bot: job #1754 completed: dist-tag rollback done. job #1755 (notify channels) queued.

sam: Thanks everyone. If jon needs any help rebuilding wheels ping me. We'll keep the change window locked until the hotfix canary is green.

jon: Uploaded 1.4.4-hotfix to PyPI and pushed artifacts to gs://ci-artifacts/sdk/1753/1.4.4-hotfix/. SHA256 verified. Link: https://pypi.org/project/redwood-sdk/1.4.4-hotfix/

sam: Verified. Canaries look good for a small cohort. Reopening change window for non-publish ops at +30m but leaving publish queue locked for another hour.

maya: I'll send the customer-facing note now and drop a short thread in #customer-success.

sam: Closing this thread — follow-up post-mortem scheduled for tomorrow 15:00 UTC. Thanks all. :clap:
